response.justification: Strong, versatile engineer with 10+ years of experience, but the profile is almost entirely web/backend (TypeScript, Node.js, DLang) rather than C++. Hands-on C++ is limited to roughly six months at National Instruments (2014–2015) plus a university thesis project, well short of the mandatory 5–10 years of Windows C++ development. There is no fixed income, capital markets, or investment banking domain exposure (RIDE Capital is fintech/investment platform work in Node/GraphQL, not capital markets systems), and no evidence of SQL Server or Oracle depth. Communication skills, testing rigor, and CI/CD experience are clear positives, but the core mandatory requirements are unmet.
strengths: Deep engineering breadth with strong TDD, CI/CD, and testing culture
Excellent communication — public talks, workshops, and courses delivered
concerns: Only ~6 months of professional C++, not 5–10 years on Windows
No fixed income, capital markets, or investment banking domain experience
SQL listed generically; no SQL Server or Oracle evidence
